title: Multi-region orchestration tradeoff canvas and policy sketch
content:
Purpose:
Quick working canvas for a policy layer that balances latency, cost, and reliability across regions and model variants. Intended for platform-engineering + SRE to iterate on a compact policy DSL and decision-tree that the control plane can evaluate cheaply at request time.

Scope and constraints:
- We only control routing at the inference-router boundary (not full network routing) — i.e., choose region + model-variant + capacity-tier per request.
- Hard SLOs: customer-configurable latency SLO (p50/p95), reliability floor (e.g., >=99.9%), cost budget per 1e6 tokens or per-request.
- Runtime restrictions: evaluation must be O(1) or very small constant-time; complex optimization runs offline.
- Default policy should be simple and debuggable; advanced heuristics live behind feature flags.

High-level idea (traffic compass):
- Compute three normalized scores for each candidate target: latency_score, cost_score, reliability_score.
- Apply user/team weights (w_latency, w_cost, w_reliability) to produce a utility = w_latency*latency_score + w_cost*cost_score + w_reliability*reliability_score.
- Enforce absolute gates first (latency_gate, reliability_gate, capacity_gate). Candidates failing gates are excluded.
- Choose highest-utility candidate; if utility gap < epsilon, prefer lower cost variant that meets SLO.

Score normalization sketches (cheap approximations):
- latency_score = clamp( (SLO_ms - predicted_latency_ms) / SLO_ms , -1, 1 ) 
  - predicted_latency_ms = regional_hist.p50 * scaling_by_seq_len + dynamic_node_penalty
- cost_score = 1 - normalized_cost (lower cost -> higher score); normalized_cost = (estimated_cost - min_cost) / (max_cost - min_cost)
- reliability_score = historical_success_rate_month_to_date (0..1) scaled to -1..1: 2*rate - 1

Candidate metadata required (per route):
- region, model_variant, q_profile (quant/amp), capacity_tier (dedicated/shared), p50/p95 latency, tokens_per_second_throughput, unit_cost_per_token, recent_error_rate, circuit_state (open/closed/degraded), available_slots_estimate (from capacity oracle)

Gates (examples):
- latency_gate: predicted_latency_ms <= SLO_ms * latency_gate_multiplier (default 1.2)
- reliability_gate: recent_success_rate >= reliability_threshold (default 0.995)
- capacity_gate: available_slots_estimate >= min_slots_needed (fail fast to avoid queuing)
- policy_blocklist: allow manual blocklist at customer or org level (for compliance/bugs)

Decision-tree (simple fallthrough ladder):
1) Filter candidates by policy_blocklist -> remove blacklisted targets.
2) Apply gates (latency, reliability, capacity). If none remain, go to fallback ladder.
3) Score remaining candidates with weighted utility. If a candidate utility > next_best + epsilon, select it.
4) If near-tie, select cheaper candidate if still meets gates.
5) Emit rationale and trace metadata for observability.

Fallback ladder (when gates remove everything):
- Step A: Relax latency_gate by +10% (one-time), re-evaluate.
- Step B: If still empty and customer allows degraded reliability, allow a low-priority degraded pool (best-effort) with circuit_state=degraded.
- Step C: If still empty, route to multi-turn proxy fallback (synthesize with cached prefix or local heuristic) and emit incident signal.
- Step D: Optional hard redirect to partner-hosted region (requires explicit whitelisting).

Control plane contract and config schema (proposal):
- policy { id, owner_team, default_weights: {latency,cost,reliability}, gates: {latency_multiplier, reliability_threshold, capacity_min}, severity (normal/strict) }
- route_target { id, region, model_name, variant, profile, telemetry_sources }
- run_config { local_overrides: bool, canary_percent, throttle_rules }
- evaluation_record { timestamp, request_id, chosen_target_id, scores: [..], gates_applied: [..], reason_code }

Lightweight pseudo-code (to implement in router):
- candidates = get_targets(route)
- candidates = candidates.filter(not_blocked)
- candidates = candidates.filter(pass_gates)
- if candidates.empty: candidates = fallback_relax_and_retry(route)
- chosen = pick_best_by_utility(candidates, weights)
- log_evaluation(chosen, candidates, weights)

Observability (what to record per request):
- chosen_target_id, candidate_list_snapshot (ids + utility values), predicted_latency_ms, actual_latency_ms, tokens_generated, error_flag, policy_id, weights_used, fallback_used boolean, decision_timestamp
- Aggregate dashboards: per-policy regret (cost above baseline), tie-rate (how often utility gaps < epsilon), fallback-rate, gate-failure-reasons (capacity vs latency vs reliability).

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for utility math, normalization edge cases, gate precedence.
- Simulation harness (offline): replay 7 days of traffic with historical telemetry and compare cost/latency/reliability tradeoffs across weight vectors. Produce pareto curves and heatmaps.
- Canary: 1% traffic, synthetic load + real traffic. Expose quick rollback via feature flag and provide automatic fallback to previous router logic if error rate delta > 0.5%.

Experiment matrix to run (offline sims):
- Vary w_cost from 0 to 1 in 0.1 steps, w_latency adjusted so sum=1 (w_reliability fixed at 0.2) -> measure mean cost, p95 latency, reliability.
- Region-skewed traffic: concentrate 60% traffic in EMEA to see capacity pressure effects.
- Burst failure injection: simulate a region node outage and observe fallback latency/regret.

Operational playbook snippets (for runbooks):
- If fallback-rate > 1% for 30m: check capacity oracle, check regional ASGs, increase dedicated pool or enable burst capacity for critical customers.
- If tie-rate > 20%: tune epsilon upward or favor cost tie-breaker to reduce oscillation.
- If policy changes cause >5% error-rate on canary: auto revert and create ticket PLAT-rollback-<ts>.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How frequently should telemetry used for predicted_latency be updated? (current thought: 30s sliding window for p50, p95 but use EMA for p50 to reduce noise)
- Should reliability_score punish spikes more than sustained small degradations? (proposal: derivative penalty for sudden spike in error rate)
- Schema for customer overrides: freeform weights vs canned profiles (low-latency, low-cost, balanced) — which is easier to support?
- Integration point with billing: best to compute cost estimates in token units at router or precomputed per-target by pricing service?

Notes to self:
- Keep default policy biased slightly toward lower-cost variants for non-critical routes; customers expecting low latency should opt-in to strict profiles.
- Keep decision trace small: only include top-3 candidates in per-request log to limit payload size.
- Coordinate with SRE on how to surface capacity oracle health to policy engine (must degrade gracefully).

Immediate next steps:
- Sync w/ Jae on capacity oracle API shape (PLAT-1124).
- Prototype utility function in python sim harness (elena will help with datasets).
- Draft a compact policy DSL doc for product review (one-pager + examples).

End of canvas.

(Loose formatting on purpose — this is a working doc. Will refine into a spec + examples once simulations produce graphs.)
